Photograph: Andrew Aitchison/In Pictures/Getty Images Kent Hundreds evacuated after fire breaks out at seaside hotel in Kent About 280 people taken to safety from the Grand Burstin in Folkestone after blaze thought to have started in basement Sammy Gecsoyler Sat 19 Sep 2026 06.44 EDT Last modified on Sat 19 Sep 2026 09.55 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Hundreds of people have been evacuated from a hotel in Folkestone after a large fire broke out overnight. Emergency services were called just after 1am on Saturday to the Grand Burstin hotel in Folkestone, where a fire is believed to have started in the basement, Kent fire and rescue service said. About 280 people were taken to safety and Folkestone and Hythe district council set up a welfare centre. No injuries relating to the fire have been reported and the cause of the blaze is not yet known. View image in fullscreen Fire damage at the hotel. Photograph: Andrew Aitchison/In Pictures/Getty Images Twenty-six fire engines were dispatched to the seafront hotel, the fire service said. According to the Britannia Hotels website, the Grand Burstin overlooks Folkestone’s harbour and has 550 rooms. Folkestone and Hythe district council posted on X: “A fire is currently ongoing at the Folkestone Grand Burstin hotel. “We are operating a welfare centre at Three Hills Sports Park for people being evacuated from the site, where we are providing support to those affected. “We are supporting all emergency services involved in the response and their efforts to get people to safety. “Our advice to residents living nearby is to: close all windows and doors; avoid the area and do not attempt to approach the hotel; follow the instructions of emergency services; keep roads clear to allow emergency vehicles to access the area.” Kent fire and rescue service said in an update: “Ten fire engines remain at the scene of a fire at the Grand Burstin hotel in The Harbour, Folkestone. “Crews wearing breathing apparatus have worked hard to bring the fire under control and are now dampening down any remaining hotspots. “It’s believed the fire started in the basement of the property, but the cause is not yet known. “Around 280 people evacuated the building, and a welfare centre has been organised by Folkestone and Hythe district council. No fire-related injuries have been reported.” A spokesperson for Kent police said: “Kent police was called at around 1.20am on Saturday 19 September 2026 to reports of a fire at a hotel on Marine Parade, Folkestone. “Officers remain in attendance to assist traffic flow while our Kent fire and rescue service colleagues work to tackle the fire.” Explore more on these topics Kent Hospitality industry Hotels Firefighters news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland

Riot officers moved forward behind shields as fires burned in the streets, and several people were detained. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT The unrest followed parliament's first reading of amendments aimed at limiting the powers of the Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague. The court recently convicted four former Kosovo Liberation Army commanders of war crimes committed during the 1998-99 conflict. The proposed changes would cap prison sentences at 15 years, allow appeals to Kosovo's Supreme Court and let convicted people serve their sentences in Kosovo. Tensions escalated after demonstrators blocked the exits of parliament and government buildings to prevent lawmakers from leaving. The proposed amendments still need a second reading and final approval.
